result.markdown: --- title: "Canadian Crop Market Analytics" subtitle: "Production, farm prices and currency exposure for grain procurement" author: "Miguelangel Palma Rojas" date: last-modified lang: en description: "A bilingual, reproducible R and SQLite case study for Canadian crop market intelligence." --- ::: {.hero-panel} This portfolio project converts four preserved agricultural and foreign-exchange datasets into a validated SQLite decision layer. It demonstrates how an analyst can move from raw snapshots to parameterized SQL, explicit units, tested business logic and an executive interpretation. ::: ## Executive snapshot ::: {.grid} ::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4} ::: {.metric-card} Largest 2020 crop Wheat 35,183,000 metric tonnes ::: ::: ::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4} ::: {.metric-card} Barley farm price CAD 220.53 per metric tonne · Dec 2020 ::: ::: ::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4} ::: {.metric-card} 250-tonne scenario CAD 55,132 farm-price estimate before logistics and contracts ::: ::: ::: ### What the evidence says - **Wheat leads national volume.** In the latest annual snapshot, Wheat is the largest of the four covered crops. - **Provincial context matters.** Alberta and Saskatchewan represent only the provincial observations included in this teaching dataset; the remainder of Canada is not decomposed. - **Currency changes the USD view.** Dividing CAD per tonne by CAD per USD provides a comparable USD estimate for months where price and FX observations overlap. - **This is a monitoring layer, not a purchasing recommendation.** Grade, freight, basis, storage, counterparties and contract terms remain outside the data. ## Decision question Canadian breweries, distilleries and food manufacturers need to monitor grain availability and farm-price exposure. This analysis asks: 1. Which covered crops dominate national production? 2. How have barley, rye and wheat volumes changed over time? 3. How much of national barley production is represented by Alberta and Saskatchewan? 4. How do Saskatchewan barley prices translate from CAD to USD? 5. What would a simple volume scenario cost before commercial adjustments? ## Data quality and coverage ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} | |Dataset | Records|First observation |Last observation | Missing cells| |:----------|:-----------|-------:|:-----------------|:----------------|-------------:| |crop |Annual crop | 672|1965-12-31 |2020-12-31 | 0| |daily_fx |Daily FX | 1,033|2017-01-03 |2021-02-18 | 0| |monthly_fx |Monthly FX | 50|2017-01-01 |2021-02-01 | 0| |prices |Farm prices | 2,678|1985-01-01 |2020-12-01 | 0| ::: ::: The committed files are dated snapshots, not live feeds. Their URLs, checksums and retrieval metadata are documented under `data/`. See the complete [data dictionary](docs/data-dictionary.md). ## Analytical architecture ```{mermaid} flowchart LR A[Validated CSV snapshots] --> B[(Temporary SQLite)] B --> C[Versioned SQL files] C --> D[R analytical functions] D --> E[English report] D --> F[Spanish report] G[testthat] --> B G --> C H[GitHub Actions] --> G H --> E H --> F ``` The database is recreated during every run. Composite indexes support the crop–geography–time access patterns, while parameterized queries keep user-supplied values outside SQL text. The full model is documented in [Analytical architecture](docs/architecture.md). ## National production ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/latest-production-1.png){fig-alt='Bar chart comparing Canadian production of wheat, canola, barley and rye in 2020.' width=672} ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/production-trends-1.png){fig-alt='Lines showing Canadian barley, rye and wheat production from 1965 to 2020.' width=672} ::: ::: Long-run volume provides supply context, but it does not represent inventory available for immediate purchase. Production also needs to be interpreted alongside grade, regional concentration and logistics. ## Provincial barley context ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Covered province | Production (metric tonnes)| Share of Canada (%)| |:----------------|--------------------------:|-------------------:| |Alberta | 5,283,000| 49.2| |Saskatchewan | 4,385,100| 40.8| ::: ::: The shares do not sum to 100% because the source includes only Alberta, Saskatchewan and the Canadian total. That constraint is made explicit instead of treating the two provinces as a complete provincial breakdown. ## Price and currency exposure ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/price-history-1.png){fig-alt='Lines comparing Saskatchewan barley farm prices in Canadian and US dollars from 2017 to 2020.' width=672} ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Month | CAD / tonne| CAD per USD| USD / tonne| |:----------|-----------:|-----------:|-----------:| |2020-12-01 | 220.53| 1.2808| 172.19| |2020-11-01 | 210.63| 1.3068| 161.18| |2020-10-01 | 209.91| 1.3215| 158.85| |2020-09-01 | 211.70| 1.3228| 160.04| |2020-08-01 | 208.87| 1.3222| 157.97| |2020-07-01 | 204.45| 1.3498| 151.46| ::: ::: The conversion is an analytical estimate based on monthly average FX, not an executable foreign-exchange quote. ## Procurement scenario ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Crop |Province |Price month | Volume (t)| CAD / t| USD / t| Estimated CAD| Estimated USD| |:------|:------------|:-----------|----------:|-------:|-------:|-------------:|-------------:| |Barley |Saskatchewan |2020-12-01 | 250| 220.53| 172.19| 55,132.5| 43,047.5| ::: ::: ::: {.callout-warning title="Interpretation boundary"} This scenario multiplies observed farm price by volume. It excludes freight, quality premiums or discounts, storage, taxes, hedging, financing and negotiated terms. It is useful for sensitivity analysis—not for placing an order. ::: ## SQL as a versioned analytical asset The report no longer hides important queries inside notebook chunks. They live under [`sql/`](sql/) and are called by tested functions in [`R/analysis.R`](R/analysis.R). ```sql WITH latest_production AS ( SELECT YEAR AS production_year, PRODUCTION AS production_metric_tonnes, AVG_YIELD AS yield_kg_per_hectare FROM crop_data WHERE GEO = 'Canada' AND CROP_TYPE = ? ORDER BY YEAR DESC LIMIT 1 ), latest_price AS ( SELECT p.DATE AS price_date, p.PRICE_PRERMT AS price_cad_per_tonne, fx.FXUSDCAD AS cad_per_usd, ROUND(p.PRICE_PRERMT / fx.FXUSDCAD, 2) AS price_usd_per_tonne FROM farm_prices AS p INNER JOIN monthly_fx AS fx ON p.DATE = fx.DATE WHERE p.CROP_TYPE = ? AND p.GEO = ? ORDER BY p.DATE DESC LIMIT 1 ) SELECT * FROM latest_production CROSS JOIN latest_price; ``` ## Reproduce the project ```bash Rscript -e "if (!requireNamespace('renv', quietly = TRUE)) install.packages('renv')" Rscript -e "renv::restore()" Rscript data-raw/prepare-data.R # optional: refresh the preserved snapshots Rscript tests/testthat.R quarto render ``` GitHub Actions executes validation, tests and a full bilingual render for every pull request. The generated website is uploaded as a workflow artifact. ## Conclusion The strongest market signal in the covered data is the scale difference between wheat and the other crops, while Saskatchewan and Alberta provide useful—but incomplete—regional context. The price/FX join adds a procurement-oriented currency view, and the scenario layer makes assumptions auditable. A production decision would still require current quotes, delivered-cost modeling, grades, logistics and contract terms. Continue with the [Spanish version](es/index.qmd) or inspect the [source and methodology](https://github.com/MPalma21/canadian-crop-sql-analytics).
